title: How much is left after the electric bill is paid?
description: A bank account holds one hundred and sixty rupees, and an electric bill of thirty rupees is paid from it. Money taken out is a debit, and it is taken away from the balance. Keeko mistakes a debit for money added.
teaching_notes: One idea: a debit is money going out, so it is a negative number and the balance goes down. Watch for students who add the debit to the balance.

source: The next day you pay your electric bill of ₹30 using your bank account (a 'debit').
video_script.why: The child takes a debit away from the bank balance and sees a debit as a negative number.
video_script.substitution: Write the debit as a negative number and take it away from the balance.
video_script.wrong_move: adds the debit to the balance instead of taking it away, because the amount looks like money
video_script.payoff_line: The balance is now one hundred and thirty rupees.
maths_rules: a debit of ₹30 is money going out: −30
video_script.design: One idea: a debit is a negative number and it is taken away from the balance. The passbook from the last video now shows a payment going out. Keeko adds the debit, and the money leaving the bank shows the slip.
